record.title: DataSpace reports large harness-dependent accuracy differences on heterogeneous data-agent tasks
record.summary: The paper introduces DataSpace, a benchmark for data agents that must combine evidence scattered across heterogeneous task workspaces and return complete, verifiable tables. Its 410 cross-language tasks use 7,439 artifacts totaling 15.01 GB across six file and media types. In author-run comparisons, six backbones reach a best accuracy of 66.34% with DataSpace-Agent fixed; with MiMo-V2.5 fixed, five harnesses range from 30.98% to 46.34%, a 15.36-point spread. Authors also report that multimodal evidence integration and joins reduce accuracy across all tested backbones, and that 76 tasks are missed by all six. The comparison shows material harness sensitivity in this benchmark, not that harness choice generally dominates model choice. The results remain paper-reported, benchmark-bounded and unreproduced.
organizations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: DataSpace is a benchmark of 410 cross-language tasks over task-local heterogeneous workspaces, with 7,439 artifacts totaling 15.01 GB across CSV, JSON, SQLite, Markdown, PDF and video; the task output is a complete verifiable table.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: With MiMo-V2.5 fixed, the authors report task accuracy from 30.98% for Smolagents to 46.34% for Grok Build, a 15.36 percentage-point spread across five tested harnesses. With DataSpace-Agent fixed, the best of six tested backbones reaches 66.34%.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that multimodal evidence integration and joins reduce accuracy across all six tested backbones; 76 of 410 tasks are missed by every backbone in the reported comparison.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The benchmark does not establish that harness choice generally matters more than model choice, nor that the measured spread transfers to other datasets, model versions, harness configurations or live organizational analytics.

evidence_gaps.description: The task benchmark and reported model/harness rankings have not been independently reproduced.
The separate fixed-backbone and fixed-harness comparisons do not identify the model-by-harness interaction across all tested combinations.
Transfer to live organizational workspaces and user utility is not measured by exact-table benchmark accuracy.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated, a 15.36-point harness spread with a fixed backbone would materially affect how data-agent systems are evaluated and optimized, and a verified heterogeneous-workspace benchmark could expose failures hidden by structured-query-only tests. The evidence is one author-run 410-task benchmark, and the spread is specific to tested systems, versions and task distribution.
limitations: All benchmark construction and model results are reported in one paper; no independent reproduction was located or run.
The 15.36-point harness spread is measured on one 410-task benchmark, one fixed MiMo-V2.5 backbone and five specific systems/versions.
The separate backbone comparison fixes DataSpace-Agent; the two experiment blocks do not estimate a full model-by-harness interaction.
Task content and artifact distribution bound external validity; live organizational analytics may differ in data quality, access and user behavior.
Benchmark accuracy measures complete-table correctness and does not measure user utility, safe access control or operational reliability in deployment.
organizations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
brief.summary: The paper introduces DataSpace, a benchmark for data agents that must combine evidence scattered across heterogeneous task workspaces and return complete, verifiable tables. Its 410 cross-language tasks use 7,439 artifacts totaling 15.01 GB across six file and media types. In author-run comparisons, six backbones reach a best accuracy of 66.34% with DataSpace-Agent fixed; with MiMo-V2.5 fixed, five harnesses range from 30.98% to 46.34%, a 15.36-point spread. Authors also report that multimodal evidence integration and joins reduce accuracy across all tested backbones, and that 76 tasks are missed by all six. The comparison shows material harness sensitivity in this benchmark, not that harness choice generally dominates model choice. The results remain paper-reported, benchmark-bounded and unreproduced.

technical.claimed_result: Across 410 tasks, the authors report 66.34% accuracy for Grok 4.5 with DataSpace-Agent fixed. With MiMo-V2.5 fixed, harness accuracy is 46.34% for Grok Build, 44.63% for Claude Code, 39.27% for DataSpace-Agent, 34.88% for Codex and 30.98% for Smolagents. They report 76 tasks missed by all six backbones and consistent degradation from multimodal evidence integration and joins.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint describes the benchmark, evaluation protocol and reported comparisons. the research desk did not execute the benchmark or reproduce results; performance measurements remain author-reported.
technical.mechanism: DataSpace turns executable analytics resources into task-local workspaces containing multiple artifact types. Agents receive a question and workspace and return the full requested table. A deterministic evaluator aligns columns, normalizes types and precision, and compares rows while rejecting incomplete or incorrect results.
technical.regime: 410 cross-language analytics tasks, 7,439 task-local artifacts and six modalities. Backbone comparisons hold DataSpace-Agent fixed across six models. Harness comparisons hold MiMo-V2.5 fixed across five tested systems and versions. Tasks are evaluated by complete-table exactness with semantics-aware normalization.
technical.reproducibility: The paper describes deterministic construction and evaluation, but this review did not execute code or independently reproduce benchmark results.
technical.strongest_baseline: For harness comparison, the fixed MiMo-V2.5 backbone with Smolagents reports 30.98% accuracy; Grok Build reports 46.34%. For backbone comparison with DataSpace-Agent fixed, GPT-5.6 Sol reports 64.63% and Grok 4.5 reports 66.34%. These are separate controlled blocks, not a factorial estimate of model-by-harness effects.

brief.title: DataSpace reports large harness-dependent accuracy differences on heterogeneous data-agent tasks
brief.why_it_matters: Data-agent evaluations that isolate SQL, retrieval or open-ended answers can miss failures when an agent must locate, reconcile and join evidence across databases, files, documents and media. A benchmark with deterministic complete-table scoring can make such failures easier to compare. The reported harness spread suggests that integrated agent design affects outcomes in this task regime, but does not establish a universal ranking or live-workplace performance.
